To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) summative ELP assessment policies and practices should be based on the best available evidence; (b) summative EPL assessments should be used in conjunction with other measures of student learning and growth; and (c) the design and implementation of summative ELP tests should reflect the diversity and needs of ELs.

(a) ELP assessments for accountability purposes should be designed and implemented with a clear and coherent purpose in mind; (b) ELP assessment policies should be informed by research and practice, including the perspectives of stakeholders; and (c) ELP assessment research should focus on the development, implementation, and use of ELP assessments, including how they are used in practice and how they impact students and their families.
• Summative assessments for accountability purposes are a major driver for ELP assessment systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of ELP assessments that can be used for accountability and that are aligned with the Common Core State Standards for ELs.
the design, development, and implementation of next-generation EDP assessments for K–2 ELs that are fair, valid, and reliable, as well as with the policies and practices that support them.

the development of ELP assessment systems that are more valid, reliable, and equitable and that provide actionable information to support ELs in meeting the Common Core State Standards and other college- and career-ready standards.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
summative ELP assessment systems are in need of improvement.
there is a need to develop a better understanding of the nature of ELP, the assessment of ELP, and the use of assessment results to inform instructional decisions for ELs.
summative ELP assessment policies and practices should be based on a strong theoretical foundation, be informed by research, and be aligned with the goals and purposes of ELP assessment systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ELP assessments should be used for accountability purposes and that they should be aligned with state standards, be accessible to all students, provide a valid measure of ELP, and provide useful information for educators and policymakers.
ELP assessments should be designed to provide information about ELP for the benefit of EL students.
we are in an exciting time in ELP assessment, and there are many opportunities for improvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field of ELP assessment is in a state of flux, and there are many opportunities to advance research, practice, and policy in ways that will benefit EL students.
we need a more nuanced and comprehensive understanding of ELP, one that goes beyond a focus on English language skills and includes the development and use of academic English.
we need to work together to ensure that ELP assessment results are used for accountability purposes in ways that support the educational success of EL students.
